_comment: Narration for the < 3 min demo. Each segment = one caption + one voice clip. 'scene' tells web/demo.js what to show. Edit text here, then run scripts/make_voice.py to regenerate audio, SRT and the CapCut (剪映) script.

segments.text: Japan has fifteen million manhole covers. Thousands are works of art, cast in iron by the town they belong to.
segments.caption: Japan has 15 million manhole covers. Thousands are works of art, cast in iron by the town they belong to.

segments.text: Since 2016, sewer agencies have turned them into free manhole cards, each with the cover, its coordinates, and its story.
segments.caption: Since 2016, sewer agencies have turned them into free manhole cards, each with the cover, its coordinates, and its story.

segments.text: One rule: you can't buy them or order them online. You walk up to one specific counter, in one town, and ask.
segments.caption: One rule: no buying, no online orders. You walk up to one specific counter, in one town, and ask.

segments.text: That makes them perfect for travellers: a free souvenir, and a reason to step off the tourist trail. Many counters are tourist offices you'd pass anyway.
segments.caption: That makes them perfect for travellers: a free souvenir, and a reason to step off the tourist trail. Many counters are on your way anyway.

segments.text: But the official list is forty-seven pages of Japanese addresses, with no map. So we built one.
segments.caption: But the official list is 47 pages of Japanese addresses, with no map. So we built one.

segments.text: Manhole Pilgrim. Every card in Japan, on one map.
We geocoded all thirteen hundred counters with Amazon Location Places: Geocode for addresses, Search Text for places with only a name.
segments.caption: All 1,313 counters geocoded with Amazon Location Places: Geocode for addresses, SearchText for name-only places.

segments.text: Ten years of releases. Series one had thirty cards. Every few months a new series lands, until all forty-seven prefectures are covered.
segments.caption: Ten years of releases. Series 1 (April 2016): 30 cards. Every few months a new series lands, until all 47 prefectures are covered.

segments.text: Click any card to see its design, where to pick it up, and the opening hours, with a link to the official page.
segments.caption: Click any card for the design, the counter, opening hours, and a link to the official page.

segments.text: Filter by where you pick them up. One card in five is only handed out at a sewage or water plant. The cards were built to bring people into infrastructure they never see.
segments.caption: 1 in 5 cards is only handed out at a sewage or water plant. The cards bring people into infrastructure they never see.

segments.text: Now the traveller's question: I'm in Kyoto this weekend, how many can I collect? Calculate Isolines draws the real one-hour drive area. About a hundred cards fall inside.
segments.caption: "I'm in Kyoto this weekend. How many can I collect?" CalculateIsolines draws the real 1-hour drive area: {reach} cards inside.

segments.text: Optimize Waypoints turns the six nearest into a loop with arrival times. That is an easy afternoon, and six cards you can only get here.
segments.caption: OptimizeWaypoints turns the six nearest into a loop with arrival times. An easy afternoon, and six cards you can only get here.

segments.text: Some starts, like the middle of Sapporo Station, can't be driven back to. Then the app falls back to a route matrix and plans a one-way trip on real drive times.
segments.caption: Can't drive back to the start? The app falls back to CalculateRouteMatrix and a one-way plan on real drive times.

segments.text: The map also surprised us. The loneliest card is on the Ogasawara Islands, nine hundred kilometres from any other.
segments.caption: The loneliest card: Ogasawara Islands, 898 km from any other.

segments.text: And this Hyogo card can only be collected in Osaka. Our geocoder flagged it as an error. It wasn't. The treatment plant sits across the border.
segments.caption: A Hyōgo card you can only get in Osaka. Our geocoder flagged it as an error. It wasn't: the plant sits across the border.

segments.text: Ninety-eight cards wait at michi-no-eki roadside stations. Manhole cards are a road-trip game.
segments.caption: 98 cards wait at michi-no-eki roadside stations. Manhole cards are a road-trip game.

segments.text: How it works: scrape the registry, geocode with Amazon Location, merge into an Apache Iceberg table on S3 with Athena, and serve a static site on Amplify. Maps and Routes run in the browser, with no backend.
Each series is an Iceberg snapshot you can time-travel to. Swap the scraper, and it works for any stamp rally.
segments.caption: Every series is an Iceberg snapshot: FOR VERSION AS OF series 1 returns 30 cards. Swap the scraper to reuse it for any stamp rally.

segments.text: Manhole Pilgrim. Go find the sewers.
